title: Strategy & Decision Making Adventure 2: Generic Strategies & Blue Ocean
welcome_lead: Today you'll pick a generic strategy (Porter) or sail into a blue ocean.
meta_desc: IBDP Business Management Strategy: Porter generic strategies (cost leadership, differentiation, focus) and blue ocean.
final_note: You distinguished Porter's three generic strategies and the blue ocean approach.

concepts.def: Failing to choose, weak on both

walkthroughs.body_html:
Porter (1985) said firms must choose.

Cost leadership: lowest cost across the industry (Walmart, Ryanair).
Differentiation: unique attributes (Apple, BMW).
Focus: a narrow segment, either cost or differentiation (Rolls-Royce).

Trying both risks being stuck in the middle.

Kim & Mauborgne (2005) propose escaping the bloody 'red ocean' of competition by creating new market space.

Examples: Cirque du Soleil reinvented circus; Nintendo Wii targeted casual gamers.

Key tools: ERRC grid — Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create.

The right strategy fits resources and industry context.

A small firm without economies of scale should differentiate or focus, not chase cost leadership.

Blue ocean requires creativity and risk tolerance — most firms still battle in red oceans.
